- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction starting from day of sentiment reversal.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; add 1–2 days of smoothing or delay in forecast adjustment if sentiment is trending.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average to dampen noise and align with sentiment direction.
